summary: Caroline Humphrey is an Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies scholar. She earned degrees at Girton College and the University of Cambridge under Edmund Leach, and Leeds. She held posts at Cambridge (1978–2010), Girton, and SPRI.

Caroline Rhys Davids was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She studied at UCL under George Croom Robertson, Reinhold Rost, and T. W. Rhys Davids. She held positions at Manchester, SOAS, and the Pali Text Society.

Carolyn Woodford Schmidt is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington and held posts at Ohio State University and Denison University.
Carson T. Schütze is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1992 to 1997. He took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles, in 1997.

Catherine Bell was a scholar of religious studies and sinology. She studied at the University of Chicago under Joseph M. Kitagawa (~1976–1983) and served as the Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University (1985–2008).

Catherine Cornille works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at KU Leuven and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, later serving as Associate Professor of Comparative Theology at Boston College (attested ~2005).

Catherine Ella Blanshard Asher was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. She earned her PhD at the University of Minnesota (~1977–1984), where she also served as an Assistant Professor from ~1980 to 2023.

Catherine Ludvik is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. She earned her PhD from the University of Toronto under David Waterhouse. She has held teaching and research posts at Stanford, Doshisha, Kyoto Sangyo, and Hanazono.

Catherine Prueitt is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. She studied at the University of Rochester and Emory University under John D. Dunne and Laurie L. Patton, and was appointed Assistant Professor at the University of British Columbia.
Cathy Cantwell is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her PhD from the University of Kent in 1989 and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

Cecil Bendall was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cambridge and Oxford under Edward Byles Cowell and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at the British Museum, University College London, and Cambridge.

Cecil Y. Lang studied at Duke University (~1937–1941). He held academic posts at Yale University (~1949–1959), the University of Chicago (~1967–1970), and served as Professor of English at the University of Virginia (~1970–1991).

Ch'ing-mao Cheng is a scholar of Sinology and Japanology who studied at National Taiwan University and Princeton University. He held positions at UC Berkeley, UMass Amherst, and served as Founding Chair at National Dong Hwa University.

Chack-fan Lee, active in Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Hong Kong (~1964–1968) and the University of Western Ontario (~1969–1972). He served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor at the University of Hong Kong from 1994 to 2015.
Chaesong Kim is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Kim completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo (attested 1995), studying under Yasunori Ejima.

Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under numerous teachers, including Delog Dawa Drolma, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Tromge Trungpa Rinpoche, Khenpo Dorje, Jangchub Dorje, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Chaim Rabin was a linguist who studied at SOAS University of London and the University of Oxford (Christ Church). He held posts at the University of Oxford (1941–1956) and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1956–1986).

Chaisit Suwanvarangkul is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held researcher posts at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi, and served as Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2015).

Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad is a philosopher, Indologist, and religious studies scholar. He completed a doctorate at Oxford, held research fellowships at Trinity College, Oxford and Clare Hall, Cambridge, and became a Distinguished Professor at Lancaster University.

Chamnong Adivadhanasit is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA from Chulalongkorn University. He served as a Professor at Kasetsart University and a part-time instructor at Chulalongkorn University (both attested 2012).
